  • Any legal proceedings in respect of any matter of claim / dispute arising out of this advertisement and / or an application in response thereto can be instituted only in Mumbai and courts / tribunals / forums at Mumbai only shall have sole and exclusive jurisdiction to try any clause / dispute.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely at any stage.
  • Candidates are advised in their own interest that they should not furnish any particulars that are false, tampered with or fabricated and should not suppress any material information while submitting application. At the time of examination, interview or in a subsequent selection procedure, if a candidate is (or has been) found guilty of: (i) Using unfair means (ii) Impersonating or procuring impersonation by any person, OR (iii) Misbehaving in the examination/interview hall or disclosing, publishing, reproducing, transmitting, storing or facilitating transmission and storage of contents of the test(s) or any information therein in whole or part thereof in any form or by any means, verbal or written, electronically or mechanically for any purpose, OR (iv) Resorting to any irregular or improper means in connection with his/ her candidature, OR (v) Obtaining support for his/ her candidature by unfair means, OR (vi) Carrying mobile phones or similar electronic devices of communication in the examination/ interview hall. Such a candidate may, in addition to rendering himself/ herself liable to criminal prosecution, shall be liable; a) to be disqualified from the examination for which he/ she is a candidate: b) to be debarred either permanently or for a specified period from any examination conducted by the Bank. c) for termination of service, if he/ she has already joined the Bank.
  • CANDIDATES REPORTING LATE i.e., after the reporting time specified on the call letter for Examination will not be permitted to take the examination. The reporting time mentioned on the call letter is prior to the Start time of the test. Though the duration of the examination is 2 hours 30 minutes, candidates may be required to be at the venue for about 4 hours including the time required for completion of various formalities such as verification and collection of various requisite documents, giving of instructions, etc.
  • In the examination hall as well as at the time of interview, the call letter along with original and a photocopy of the candidate’s currently valid photo identity (bearing exactly the same name as it appears on the call letter) such as PAN Card/ Passport/ Permanent Driving License/ Voter’s Card/ Bank Passbook with photograph/ Photo identity proof issued by a Gazetted Officer on official letterhead along with photograph / Photo identity proof issued by a People’s Representative on official letterhead along with photograph / valid recent Identity Card issued by a recognized College/ University/ Aadhar card/ E-Aadhar Card with a photograph/ Employee ID/ Bar Council Identity Card with photograph should be submitted to the invigilator for verification. The candidate’s identity will be verified with respect to his/her details on the call letter, in the Attendance List and requisite documents submitted. If identity of the candidate is in doubt the candidate may not be allowed to appear for the Examination.
  • Ration Card and Learner’s Driving License are not valid id proof.
  • Note: Candidates must produce in original the photo identity proof and submit photocopy of the photo identity proof along with Examination call letter as well as the Interview Call Letter while attending the examination/ interview respectively, without which they will not be allowed to take up the examination/ interview. Candidates must note that the name as appearing on the call letter (provided during the process of registration) should exactly match the name as appearing on the photo identity proof. Female candidates who have changed first/last/middle name post marriage must take special note of this. If there is any mismatch between the name indicated in the Call Letter and Photo Identity Proof the candidate will not be allowed to appear for the examination. In case of candidates who have changed their name, will be allowed only if they produce original Gazette notification / their original marriage certificate / affidavit in original.
  • 1. The examination will be conducted at venues given in the respective call letters.
  • 2. No request for change of centre/venue/date/session for Examination shall be entertained.
  • 3. Export-Import Bank of India, however, reserves the right to cancel any of the Examination Centres and/ or add some other Centres, at its discretion, depending upon the number of candidates, administrative feasibility, etc.
  • 4. Export-Import Bank of India also reserves the right to allot the candidate to any Centre other than the one he/she has opted for.
  • 5. Candidate will appear for the examination at an Examination Centre at his/her own risks and expenses and Export-Import Bank of India will not be responsible for any injury, expense or losses etc. of any nature.
  • 6. Choice of centre once exercised by the candidate will be final. If sufficient number of candidates do not opt for a particular centre for examination, OR if the number of candidates is more than the capacity available for exam for a centre, Export-Import Bank of India reserves the right to allot any other centre to the candidate.
  • Decision of Export-Import Bank of India in all matters relating to recruitment will be final and binding on the candidate. No correspondence or personal enquiries shall be entertained by the Export-Import Bank of India in this behalf.
  • Export-Import Bank of India would be analysing the responses (answers) of individual candidates with those of other candidates to detect patterns of similarity of right and wrong answers. If in the analytical procedure adopted by Export-Import Bank of India in this regard, it is inferred/ concluded that the responses have been shared and scores obtained are not genuine/ valid, Export-Import Bank of India reserves the right to cancel the candidature of the concerned candidates and the result of such candidates (disqualified) will be withheld.
  • There will be no sectional cut off but the final list for interviews will be drawn based on the candidate’s performance in the written test.
  • Instances for providing incorrect information and/or process violation by a candidate detected at any stage of the selection process will lead to disqualification of the candidate from the selection process and he/she will not be allowed to appear in any recruitment process of Export-Import Bank of India in the future. If such instances go undetected during the current selection process but are detected subsequently, such disqualification will take place with retrospective affect.
  • A pre-recruitment training will be organised for the candidates from reserved categories. Details of the training and its mode of delivery (online / offline) will be intimated to the candidates who opt for it through the online application form. Details will be shared with such candidates after the last date of registration.
  • Candidates whose writing speed is adversely affected permanently for any reason can use their own scribe at their cost during the examination. In all such cases where a scribe is used, the following rules will apply:
  • • The candidate will have to arrange his/her own scribe at his/her own cost.
  • • The scribe arranged by the candidate should not be a candidate for the same examination. If violation of the above is detected at any stage of the process, candidature of both the candidate and the scribe will be cancelled. Candidates eligible for and who wish to use the services of a scribe in the examination should invariably carefully indicate the same in the online application form. Any subsequent request may not be favourably entertained.
  • • A person acting as a scribe for one candidate cannot be a scribe for another candidate.
  • • The scribe may be from any academic stream.
  • • Both the candidate as well as scribe will have to give a suitable undertaking confirming that the scribe fulfils all the stipulated eligibility criteria for a scribe mentioned above. Further in case it later transpires that he/she did not fulfil any laid down eligibility criteria or suppressed material facts the candidature of the applicant will stand cancelled, irrespective of the result of the examination.
  • • Those candidates who use a scribe shall be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes for every hour of the examination or as otherwise advised.
  • • Scribe should not answer on his/her own. Any such behaviour observed will result in cancellation of candidature.
  • • Only candidates registered for compensatory time will be allowed such concessions since compensatory time given to candidates shall be system based, it shall not be possible for the test conducting agency to allow such time if he / she is not registered for the same. Candidates not registered for compensatory time shall not be allowed such concessions.
  • • During the exam, at any stage, if it is found that scribe is independently answering the questions, the exam session will be terminated, and candidate’s candidature will be cancelled. The candidature of such candidates using the services of a scribe will also be cancelled if it is reported after the examination by the test administrator personnel that the scribe independently answered the questions.
  • A compensatory time of twenty minutes per hour or otherwise advised shall be permitted for the candidates with locomotor disability and cerebral palsy where dominant (writing) extremity is affected to the extent of slowing the performance of function (minimum of 40% impairment).
  • Visually Impaired candidates (who suffer from not less than 40% of disability) may opt to view the contents of the test in magnified font and all such candidates will be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes for every hour or otherwise advised of examination.
  • These guidelines are subject to change in terms of GoI guidelines/ clarifications, if any, from time to time.

How to Apply

  • Candidates need to apply online only from January 26, 2026, up to March 02, 2026. No other mode of application will be accepted.
  • Scan their: Photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm), Signature (with black ink), Left thumb impression (on white paper with black or blue ink), A handwritten declaration (on a white paper with black ink) (text given below), The consolidated Mark Sheets of Graduation and Post-Graduation, Graduation and Post-Graduation Degree, Caste Certificate (if applicable) Ensuring that all these scanned documents adhere to the required specifications as given in this Advertisement.
  • Signature in CAPITAL LETTERS will NOT be accepted.
  • The left thumb impression should be properly scanned and not smudged. (If a candidate is not having left thumb, he/she may use his/ her right thumb for applying.)
  • The text for the handwritten declaration is as follows – “I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required.”
  • The above-mentioned handwritten declaration has to be in the candidate’s handwriting and in English only. If it is written and uploaded by anybody else or in any other language, the application will be considered as invalid.
  • Keep the necessary details/documents ready to make Online Payment of the requisite application fee/ intimation charges.
  • Have a valid personal email ID and mobile no., which should be kept active till the completion of this Recruitment Process. Bank may send intimation to download call letters for the Examination etc. through the mentioned e-mail ID and / or SMS. In case a candidate does not have a valid personal e-mail ID, he/she should create his/her new e-mail ID and mobile no. before applying on-line and must maintain that email account and mobile number.
  • Candidates to visit Online Application and click on the option "APPLY ONLINE" which will open a new screen.
  • To register, choose the tab "Click here for New Registration" and enter Name, Contact details and Email-id. A Provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated by the system and displayed on the screen. Candidate should note down the Provisional Registration Number and Password. An Email & SMS indicating the Provisional Registration number and Password will also be sent.
  • In case the candidate is unable to complete the application form in one go, he / she can save the data already entered by choosing "SAVE AND NEXT" tab. Prior to submission of the online application, candidates are advised to use the "SAVE AND NEXT" facility to verify the details in the online application form and modify the same if required. Visually Impaired candidates should fill the application form carefully and verify/ get the details verified to ensure that the same are correct prior to final submission.
  • Candidates are advised to carefully fill and verify the details filled in the online application themselves as no change will be possible/ entertained after clicking the COMPLETE REGISTRATION BUTTON.
  • The Name of the candidate or his /her father/ Husband etc. should be spelt correctly in the application as it appears in the Certificates/ Mark sheets/Identity proof. Any change/alteration found may disqualify the candidature.
  • Validate your details and save your application by clicking the 'Validate your details' and 'Save & Next' button.
  • Candidates can proceed to upload Photo & Signature as per the specifications given in the Guidelines for Scanning and Upload of Photograph and Signature detailed under point "C".
  • Candidates can proceed to fill other details of the Application Form.
  • Click on the Preview Tab to preview and verify the entire application form before COMPLETE REGISTRATION.
  • Modify details, if required, and click on 'COMPLETE REGISTRATION' ONLY after verifying and ensuring that the photograph, signature uploaded and other details filled by you are correct.
  • Click on 'Payment' Tab and proceed for payment.
  • Click on 'Submit' button.
  • The application form is integrated with the payment gateway and the payment process can be completed by following the instructions.
  • The payment can be made by using Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards/ Mobile Wallets.
  • After submitting your payment information in the online application form, PLEASE WAIT FOR THE INTIMATION FROM THE SERVER. DO NOT PRESS BACK OR REFRESH BUTTON IN ORDER TO AVOID DOUBLE CHARGE.
  • On successful completion of the transaction, an e-Receipt will be generated.
  • Non-generation of 'E-Receipt' indicates PAYMENT FAILURE. On failure of payment, Candidates are advised to login again using their Provisional Registration Number and Password and repeat the process of payment.
  • Candidates are required to take a printout of the e-Receipt and online Application Form containing fee details. Please note that if the same cannot be generated, online transaction may not have been successful.
  • For Credit Card users: All charges are listed in Indian Rupee. If you use a non-Indian credit card, your bank will convert to your local currency based on prevailing exchange rates.
  • To ensure the security of your data, please close the browser window once your transaction is completed.
  • There is facility to print application form containing fee details after payment of fees.
  • While filling in the Online Application Form the candidate will be provided with separate links for uploading Photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration.
  • Click on the respective link “Upload Photograph / signature / Upload left thumb impression / handwritten declaration/ other relevant documents”.
  • Browse and select the location where the Scanned Photograph / signature / left thumb impression / handwritten declaration/ other relevant document’s file has been saved.
  • Select the file by clicking on it
  • Click the ‘Open/Upload’
  • If the file size and format are not as prescribed, an error message will be displayed.
  • Preview of the uploaded image will help to see the quality of the image. In case of unclear / smudged, the same may be re-uploaded to the expected clarity /quality.

Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026 – Complete Guide

The Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026 is designed to certify the eligibility of in-service teachers for teaching positions in Classes 1 to 8. Conducted by the Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) under the Government of Tamil Nadu, it targets working teachers appointed before a specified cutoff date. The exam is held in offline mode using OMR sheets, with two separate papers: Paper 1 for Classes 1–5 and Paper 2 for Classes 6–8.

What is Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test for Working Teachers 2026?

TET is a state-level eligibility test for teachers of Classes 1–8 in government and aided schools, ensuring they meet national standards for teaching aptitude and subject knowledge. The 2026 version includes a special focus on working teachers who have not yet cleared TET, aligning with government and Supreme Court directives to make it mandatory for all educators. Clearing TET is now essential for job security and career advancement in Tamil Nadu.

  • Conducting body: Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB), Government of Tamil Nadu
  • Level: State-level eligibility test
  • Applicable classes: Paper 1 – Classes 1–5, Paper 2 – Classes 6–8

Special TET 2026 for Working Teachers – Key Highlights

This special TET targets working teachers, offering a dedicated chance to qualify without competing with fresh candidates. It differs by restricting eligibility to in-service educators, emphasizing their need for TET clearance for promotions and regularization. The test follows the standard TNTET pattern and syllabus.

Aspect Details

Conducting body Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB), Tamil Nadu
Eligible group In-service teachers of Classes 1–8 who have not yet cleared TET
Papers Paper 1 (Classes 1–5), Paper 2 (Classes 6–8)
Mode Offline OMR-based, MCQs

Admit card download To be uploaded on TRB website; candidates advised to check regularly

Eligibility Criteria for Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test 2026 (Working Teachers)

Eligibility is limited to working teachers appointed on or before 01.09.2025 as Secondary Grade Teachers (SGT), BT Assistants, or equivalent cadres on time scale, consolidated, or part-time pay in specified departments and schools.

Educational Qualification for Paper 1 (Classes 1–5)

Candidates must possess the qualifications as per G.O.(Ms).No.13, School Education [SE3(1)] Department, dated 30.01.2020, including 10+2/HSC plus Diploma in Teacher Education/Diploma in Elementary Education or equivalent. This applies to Secondary Grade Teachers, BRTEs, and Special Education Teachers (IEDSS). In-service teachers in aided or unaided schools are also eligible if they meet NCTE norms.

Educational Qualification for Paper 2 (Classes 6–8)

Graduation in the relevant subject plus B.Ed. or equivalent, as per special rules for Tamil Nadu School Educational Subordinate Services. For Special Education Teachers, qualifications from G.O.(Ms).No.144, dated 17.06.2025 apply. Subject-specific requirements include relevant graduation for Mathematics/Science or Social Science teachers.

Age Limit and In-Service Relaxations

There is no upper age limit specified for TET eligibility. Relaxations in qualifying marks apply: 50% for BC/BCM/MBC/DNC/PWD and 40% for SC/SCA/ST.

Who Can Apply as a Working Teacher?

In-service teachers in government, government-aided, and recognized unaided private schools teaching Classes 1 to 8, including those under various departments like School Education, MBC, ADW, Tribal Welfare, and corporations. Qualified serving teachers opting for promotion must also apply.

TN TET 2026 Exam Pattern for Working Teachers

The exam pattern is identical for working and non-working candidates: 150 MCQs, 3 hours duration, no negative marking.

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Exam Pattern – Paper 1

Paper 1 is for primary level (Classes 1–5).

Section Questions Marks Medium
Child Development and Pedagogy (6–11 yrs) 30 30 Tamil/English

Language II – English 30 30 English
Mathematics 30 30 Tamil/English
Environmental Studies 30 30 Tamil/English
Total 150 150 –

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Exam Pattern – Paper 2

Paper 2 is for upper primary level (Classes 6–8).

Section Questions Marks Medium
Child Development and Pedagogy (11–14 yrs) 30 30 Tamil/English
Language I (Tamil/Telugu/Malayalam/Kannada/Urdu) 30 30 As chosen
Language II – English 30 30 English
Mathematics and Science / Social Science / Any other subject 60 60 Tamil/English
Total 150 150 –

Minimum Qualifying Marks for Working Teachers

General category: 60% (90/150). BC/BCM/MBC/DNC and PWD: 50% (75/150). SC/SCA/ST: 40% (60/150).

Tamil Nadu TET 2026 Syllabus for Working Teachers

The syllabus is based on the state-prescribed topics for Classes 1–8, with difficulty up to secondary/higher secondary stage.

TNTET 2026 Paper 1 Syllabus (Classes 1–5)

  • Child Development and Pedagogy: Stages of child development, learning theories, inclusive education, teaching–learning process, assessment and evaluation.
  • Language I (regional language): Reading comprehension, grammar, language skills, pedagogy of language development.
  • Language II – English: Comprehension, vocabulary, grammar, communication, English language pedagogy.
  • Mathematics: Number system, operations, fractions, decimals, geometry, measurement, data handling, pedagogy of mathematics.
  • Environmental Studies: Family and friends, food, water, travel, shelter, environment, resources, EVS pedagogy.

TNTET 2026 Paper 2 Syllabus (Classes 6–8)

  • Child Development and Pedagogy (11–14): Adolescent development, learning and motivation, classroom management, evaluation.
  • Language I and II: Similar components as Paper 1 but at higher difficulty level.
  • Subject-specific: Mathematics & Science – algebra, geometry, mensuration, statistics, basics of physics, chemistry, biology, pedagogy. Social Science – history, geography, civics, economics, social science pedagogy.

Note that the official TRB syllabus PDF must be followed strictly.

Application Process for Tamil Nadu Teacher Eligibility Test 2026 (Working Teachers)

Applications are online only via http://www.trb.tn.gov.in. Separate applications for Paper 1 and Paper 2 with fees.

  • Register with valid email and mobile number.
  • Fill details, upload photo (40-60 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG), signature (20-40 KB), and certificates (250-300 KB PDF).
  • Pay fee: Rs.600/- (general) or Rs.300/- (SC/SCA/ST/PWD) via net banking/credit/debit card.
  • Use edit window if needed; submit by 10-04-2026.

Documents required:

  • 10th/SSLC, 12th/HSC, Diploma/B.Ed./UG certificates and mark sheets.
  • Community certificate, Differently Abled certificate.
  • Service Certificate (Annexure-I).

Exam Centres, Hall Ticket and Exam Day Guidelines

Exams in all districts; centre details in hall ticket. Download hall ticket from TRB website. Report early with ID proof; no electronic gadgets allowed. OMR-based; follow invigilator instructions.

TN TET 2026 Result, Certificate Validity and Use for Promotions

Results published on http://www.trb.tn.gov.in as qualified lists. Qualifying candidates receive TNTET certificates. Validity is lifetime as per norms. For working teachers, TET clearance is mandatory for promotions in Tamil Nadu government schools; it's an eligibility criterion for career progression.

Benefits of Clearing Tamil Nadu TET 2026 for Working Teachers

  • Eligibility for regularization and promotions in government and aided schools.
  • Compliance with Supreme Court directions making TET mandatory for Classes 1–8 teachers.
  • Better job security and mobility, eligibility for future recruitment drives.
  • Professional recognition and alignment with national teacher quality standards.

Preparation Strategy for Working Teachers – How to Crack TN TET 2026

Balance school duties with study by focusing on pedagogy sections. Use NCERT/Tamil Nadu textbooks for content revision.

  • Create a weekly timetable around school hours.
  • Revise core concepts from textbook levels you teach daily.
  • Use weekends for full-length mock tests.
  • Focus on weak sections identified from previous attempts.

Selection Process

  • Merit list based on the average of the percentage of marks obtained in both Matriculation (with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks) and the ITI examination, with equal weightage given to both.

  • There will be no written test or viva.

How to Apply

Applicants are required to apply online by visiting www.rrc-wr.com. Detailed instructions for filling out the online application will be available on the website.

(a) Applicants are required to fill in their personal details, trade, Aadhaar number, marks/CGPA, and choice of Divisions/Workshopsetc. very carefully, as the computerized merit list will be generated solely based on the information provided in the online application. In case any discrepancy is found during document verification, the applicant shall be summarily disqualified.

(b) Though, separate slots for Stenographer(English) & PAASA are notified for Mumbai Central Division & HQ office, candidates applying for Mumbai Division and Headquarters Office will be considered through a common application. No separate application is required for Mumbai Division and Headquarters Office.

Applicants must ensure that their name, father's name, and date of birth exactly match the details recorded in their Matriculation or equivalent certificate. Any discrepancy found during Document Verification may result in cancellation of candidature and also debarment.

Applicants are advised to provide their active mobile number and valid email ID in the online application and ensure that both remain operational throughout the entire engagement process. All important notifications will be published on the official website, and email/SMS communications will be sent only to the selected applicants. Such communications shall be deemed to have been read by the applicants.

Applicants are permitted to choose only one Division/Workshop. The option once exercised shall be final and binding on the applicant. Applicants are advised to carefully refer to the trade-wise vacancy table (Annexure A) to verify the vacancies notified and ensure that the Division/Workshop they wish to apply for has available vacancies corresponding to their trade, qualification, community, and category.

Applicants possessing ITI qualifications in more than one trade may apply separately for each relevant trade.

Applicants attempting to submit more than one application for the same trade using different particulars such as Name, Father’s Name, Community, PWD status, educational and/or technical qualifications, or different Email IDs/Mobile Numbers are hereby informed that all such applications will be summarily rejected.

Applicants are required to download and retain a printout of their online application, which must be produced whenever requested by the Railway Administration.

Applicants are required to report for Document/Certificate Verification with their original documents, along with the Medical Fitness Certificate (Annexure-G), at the designated Division/Workshop/Unit.

Educational Qualification

Indian Army Agniveer Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details 

The official notification for the Indian Army Agniveer Vacancy 2026 has been released, announcing over 25,000+ (Expected) vacancies across various positions including GD, Tradesman, Technical, Soldier Pharma, and more.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates Should Posses 12TH, 10TH, 8TH Pass 

Class 10th /Matric pass with 45% marks in aggregate of five basic subjects and min 33% marks in each of those five subjects. For boards following grading system, grades commensurate to percentages, as above, will be considered. Indian Gorkhas – Class 10th simple pass.

Note: Candidates who have appeared in class 10th Board Exam and are awaiting declaration of results are also eligible to apply provided they fulfill all other Qualification Required. Such candidates, however, shall only be selected when they produce the original marksheet during the Phase II of recruitment process.

 Age Limit

  • Minimum Age: 17 ½ years
  • Maximum Age: 22 years
  • Candidates born between 01 Jul 2005 to 01 Jul 2009 (both days inclusive) are eligible to apply.

Age relaxation is applicable as per rules.

  • Upper Age limit will be relaxable upto 30 years of age (as on date of joining training) in respect of widows of Defence personnel who have died in harness.
  • Note: Women who are widowed, divorced or legally separated are also eligible provided they do not have any children subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria. Widows of Defence Personnel who have died in harness will be eligible to apply for enrolment as Women Military Police. Such widows even with children will be, however, eligible only if they have not remarried.

Physical Standards

  • Height: 162 cms.
  • Chest Expansion: The candidate should be capable of chest expansion of 05 cms.
  • Weight: Weight standards are based on BMI as per the chart below.

Special Physical Standards

Candidates belonging to following regions will be given 4 cms height relaxation:

  • North East Region: Sikkim, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Mizoram, Meghalaya and Assam.
  • Gorkhas.
  • Garhwalis.
  • Ladakher.
  • Tribals of recognized tribal areas.

Note: Domicile and Caste certificate will be considered to determine applicability of height relaxation.

Application Fee

  • Examination Fee: Rs 250/- per application for all categories.
  • Payment Mode: Online (through the website during application).

Important Dates

  • Starting Date for Apply Online: 13-02-2026
  • Last Date for Apply Online: 01-04-2026
  • Online Exam Dates: 01/06/2026 to 15/06/2026 (Tentative)
  • Firm dates for online exam will be announced later on the website.

Selection Process

  • Phase I - Online Common Entrance Exam (CEE): Conducted at Computer based test centres. This will be conducted for provisionally shortlisted candidates. Admission to the examination will be purely on the basis of Admit Card. The CEE will be conducted at designated centres tentatively between 01 Jun 2026 to 15 Jun 2026.
  • Phase II - Recruitment Rally: Proportionate to the vacancies available candidates would be shortlisted based on the aggregate marks scored in the CEE. Shortlisted candidates will attend the Recruitment Rally at designated venue where the Physical Fitness Test, Physical Measurement Test, Medical Test and Document Verification will be conducted.

Physical Fitness Test (PFT) (At Rally Site)

  • 1.6 Km Run
    • Group I: Upto 7 Min 45 Secs - Excellent
    • Group II: 7 Min 46 Sec to 8 Min 30 Sec - Good
  • Long Jump: 10 Feet (Need to qualify)
  • High Jump: 3 Feet (Need to qualify)

Note: Provisions for extra time for 1.6 Km run in hilly terrain and lower timing for Long Jump and High Jump in such cases.

Medical Standards

  • Candidates must be in good physical and mental health, free from any disability likely to interfere with efficient performance of duties.
  • Detailed medical examination as per Army standards.

Final Merit List

  • Final merit list will be based on aggregate of marks scored in CEE and performance in PFT (if applicable).
  • Recruitment is purely based on merit depending on available vacancies.

Note: Selection in the Indian Army is 'Fair & Transparent' and on merit only. At no stage any bribe is to be paid to anyone for selection or recruitment in the Indian Army. Candidates should not fall prey to unscrupulous persons posing as recruiting agents.

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official website: www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.
  2. If new user, complete the registration process by providing basic details and creating a login ID.
  3. Login using the credentials and fill the online application form carefully.
  4. Upload required documents, photographs, and signatures as per specifications.
  5. Pay the examination fee of Rs 250/- online.
  6. Submit the application and take a printout for future reference.

Note: Applications invited from domiciles of all districts of Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, UT of Chandigarh & Delhi. Any change in policy or details published in notification will be intimated on registered email/mobile number and with a ticker on the www.joinindianarmy.nic.in web portal.

Documents Required

Candidates must carry the following documents in original along with self-attested photocopies at the rally site (Phase II):

  • Admit Card.
  • 20 copies of passport size photographs.
  • Education Certificates (Marksheets, Degree, etc.).
  • Domicile Certificate.
  • Caste Certificate (if applicable for relaxation).
  • Religion Certificate (if required).
  • School Character Certificate.
  • Character Certificate from Village Sarpanch/Municipal Corporation.
  • Unmarried Certificate.
  • NCC Certificate (if applicable).
  • Sports Certificate (if applicable).
  • Affidavit on Rs 10 stamp paper as per format.
  • Single Bank A/C, PAN Card & AADHAR Card.
  • Police Verification Form.
  • Certificate from serving personnel for wards of serving soldiers (if applicable).
  • Any other relevant documents as specified in the notification.

Salary Structure

Agniveers will be paid a customized package with fixed yearly increment. In addition, Risk and Hardship, Ration, Dress and Travel allowances as applicable.

  • Post: Assistant Commandants (Group A) in Central Armed Police Forces
  • Pay Scale: Details not mentioned in the notification
  • Candidates will receive salary and allowances as per Government of India rules applicable to Group A officers in Central Armed Police Forces
  • The selected candidates will be appointed in BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, or SSB based on their merit rank and force preference

Age Limit (as on 01-08-2026)

  • Minimum Age: 20 years (must have been born not later than 1st August, 2006)
  • Maximum Age: 25 years (must have been born not earlier than 2nd August, 2001)
  • Age Relaxation:
    • SC/ST candidates: Up to a maximum of 5 years
    • OBC candidates: Up to a maximum of 3 years (for those eligible to avail reservation)
    • Civilian Central Government Servants/Ex-Servicemen: Up to a maximum of 5 years in accordance with existing Central Government instructions (total relaxation limited to 5 years)
    • SC/ST and OBC candidates who are also Civilian Central Government Servants/Ex-servicemen: Eligible for cumulative age-relaxation under both categories
  • Important Notes on Age:
    • The date of birth accepted is that entered in the Matriculation or Secondary School Leaving Certificate or equivalent certificate
    • No other document relating to age (Horoscopes, Affidavits, Birth extracts from Municipal Corporation, Service records) will be accepted
    • Once Date of Birth has been submitted in the Online Application Form, no change will be allowed subsequently on any grounds whatsoever
    • Save as provided above, the age limits prescribed can in no case be relaxed

Application Fee

Category Application Fee
General/OBC/EWS (Male Candidates) Rs. 200/- (Rupees Two Hundred only)
All Female Candidates / SC / ST Candidates NIL (Exempted from payment of fee)
  • Payment Mode: Fee can be paid either by using Net Banking Facility of any Bank or by using Visa/Master/RuPay/Credit/Debit Card/UPI Payment only
  • Payment of fee through any other mode is neither valid nor acceptable
  • Applications submitted without the prescribed fee/mode (unless remission of fee is claimed) shall be summarily rejected
  • Fee once paid shall not be refunded under any circumstances nor can the fee be held in reserve for any other examination or selection
  • Important: No fee exemption is available to OBC/EWS candidates and they are required to pay the full prescribed fee

Important Dates

Event Date / Time
Notification Date 20/02/2026
Start Date of Online Application 20/02/2026
Last Date of Online Application 12/03/2026 (till 18:00 hours)
Written Examination Date 19th July, 2026
Written Exam Timing - Paper-I 10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon
Written Exam Timing - Paper-II 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM
e-Admit Card Download Date Last working day of preceding week of examination date
Physical Standards Tests / Physical Efficiency Tests After declaration of Written Exam result
Interview / Personality Test After PST/PET (for qualified candidates)
Medical Standards Tests After Interview / Personality Test

Selection Process

  • Stage 1: Written Examination (19th July, 2026)
    • Paper-I: General Ability and Intelligence - 250 Marks
      • Duration: 2 hours (10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon)
      • Type: Objective (Multiple Choice) Type questions
      • Medium: English as well as Hindi
      • Subjects: General Mental Ability (logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, numerical ability, data interpretation), General Science, Current Events of National & International Importance, Indian Polity & Economy, History of India, Indian & World Geography
      • There will be penalty (Negative Marking) for wrong answers: One third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question will be deducted for each wrong answer
    • Paper-II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension - 200 Marks
      • Duration: 3 hours (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM)
      • Type: Conventional (Descriptive) Type
      • Part-A: Essay questions (80 Marks) - to be answered in long narrative form either in Hindi or English. Topics: modern Indian history especially freedom struggle, geography, polity and economy, security and human rights issues, analytical ability
      • Part-B: Comprehension, précis writing, other communications/language skills (120 Marks) - to be attempted in English only. Topics: Comprehension passages, précis writing, developing counter arguments, simple grammar and other language testing aspects
      • Candidates must write answers only in the medium allowed. No credit for answers written in other medium
    • There will be minimum qualifying marks separately in each Paper as may be fixed by the Commission
    • Paper-I will be evaluated first and Paper-II will be evaluated only for those who obtain minimum qualifying marks in Paper-I
  • Stage 2: Physical Standards Tests (PST) / Physical Efficiency Tests (PET)
    • Conducted for candidates qualified in Written Examination
    • Physical Standards Requirements:
      • Men: Height 165 cm, Chest 81 cm (unexpanded) with 5 cm minimum expansion, Weight 50 kg
      • Women: Height 157 cm, Weight 46 kg
      • Height and chest measurement will be measured correct to one decimal in centimeter
      • Weight should be as per height and age as per prescribed chart
    • Physical Efficiency Tests:
      • Men: 100 Meter Race in 16 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 3 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.5 Meters (3 Chances), Shot Put (7.26 Kg) 4.5 Meters (3 Chances)
      • Women: 100 Meter Race in 18 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 4 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.0 Meters (3 Chances)
    • Female candidates must submit self-declaration about pregnancy status before PST/PET
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Stage 3: Interview / Personality Test
    • Only for candidates qualified in PST/PET
    • Marks: 150 Marks
    • Conducted by Union Public Service Commission
    • Candidates declared unqualified in PET will not be called for Interview
    • NCC 'B' or 'C' Certificate holders will be given consideration at Interview stage
  • Stage 4: Medical Standards Tests (MST)
    • Conducted only for candidates who appeared in Interview/Personality Test
    • Detailed Medical Standards prescribed for Eye Sight, Ear, Nose, Neck, Teeth, General Health, etc.
    • Eye Sight: Better eye 6/6 or 6/9 (corrected), Worse eye 6/12 or 6/9 (corrected), Near Vision N6/N9 (corrected), Colour Perception CP-III by ISIHARA plates
    • LASIK surgery correction permitted subject to prescribed criteria
    • Candidates declared 'UNFIT' can appear before Review Medical Board preferably next day of DME
    • Appeals against MST results must be made within 24 hours after declaration of DME results
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Final Selection/Merit:
    • Merit list drawn on basis of marks obtained in Written Examination and Interview/Personality Test
    • Any candidate found not satisfying prescribed Medical Standards after MST will not be appointed
    • Tie Breaking Principle: (i) Higher marks in written total, (ii) Higher marks in Paper-I, (iii) Senior in age, (iv) At Commission's discretion

How to Apply

  • Candidates are required to apply online only using the Commission's website: https://upsconline.nic.in
  • No other mode is allowed for submission of application
  • Application Process has Four Modules:
    • Module 1: Account Creation - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams)
    • Module 2: Universal Registration (URN) - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams). URN generated is unique and remains constant for all UPSC exams
    • Module 3: Common Application Form (CAF) - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams)
    • Module 4: Examination Specific Module - Can be filled only during notification period (includes fees, centres, force preferences, etc.)
  • Documents Required:
    • Recent passport-size colour photograph (scanned in .jpg format, 20 KB to 200 KB)
    • Signature (scanned - sign three times one below other on plain white paper using black ink, .jpg format, 20 KB to 100 KB)
    • Live photograph (to be captured while filling CAF)
    • One Photo ID Card details (Aadhaar/Voter/PAN/Passport/Driving License/Any other Government Photo ID)
    • Date of Birth certificate (Matriculation/Secondary School Leaving Certificate)
    • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
    • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in prescribed format, if applicable
    • OBC candidates: OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate based on income for FY 2024-25, 2023-24, 2022-23, issued on/after 01.04.2025 but not later than 12.03.2026
    • EWS candidates: EWS Certificate based on income for FY 2024-25, issued on/after 01.04.2025 but not later than 12.03.2026
    • Ex-servicemen: Prescribed Certificate and Undertaking as per Appendix-VI(A) and VI(B)
  • Read General Instructions, Profile/Module-wise Instructions, and Instructions for uploading documents carefully before filling the form
  • Prepare requisite documents in advance for smooth flow during form filling
  • Pay application fee (if applicable) through Net Banking/Credit/Debit Card/UPI
  • Select examination centre from available options (first-apply-first-allot basis)
  • Indicate force preferences (BSF/CRPF/CISF/ITBP/SSB)
  • Review all entered information carefully before final submission
  • Take printout or save soft copy of submitted application for future reference
  • Last Date: 12th March, 2026 (till 18:00 hours)
  • Candidates are strongly advised to apply online well in time without waiting for the last date
  • After Written Exam Result: Qualified candidates must login within 15 days window and update details/educational qualification status with proof, failing which will not be allowed in further stages
  • Download e-Admit Card from Commission's website on last working day of preceding week of examination
  • No Admit Card will be sent by post or email

  • Senior Officer – CBG Operations (3.9): 4-year full-time regular engineering course in any branch AND 2-year full-time regular ME/MTech – Biotechnology.
  • Senior Officer – CGD Operations & Maintenance / Projects (3.10, 3.11): 4-year full-time regular engineering course in Mechanical / Electrical / Instrumentation / Civil Engineering.

  • Deputy General Manager – Polymer Export (3.24): 2-year full-time regular MBA course in Sales / Marketing / Operations / Supply Chain AND Minimum 3-year full-time graduation in any discipline.

  • Manager / Senior Manager – IS (Enterprise Architect) (3.28): 4-year full-time regular engineering course in Computer Science and Engineering OR full-time Masters in Computer Applications (MCA).
  • Assistant Manager / Manager / Senior Manager – HR (3.29): 2-year full-time Post Graduate Degree / Equivalent course in HR / Personnel Management / Industrial Relations / Psychology or MBA with specialization in HR.

Desirable: 2-year full-time regular Masters in Cyber Security / Information Security / OT Security.

  • Pay Scale ₹50,000 – ₹1,60,000: CTC Approx. ₹18.14 Lakh per annum
  • Pay Scale ₹60,000 – ₹1,80,000: CTC Approx. ₹21.77 Lakh per annum
  • Pay Scale ₹70,000 – ₹2,00,000: CTC Approx. ₹26.24 Lakh per annum
  • Pay Scale ₹80,000 – ₹2,20,000: CTC Approx. ₹29.98 Lakh per annum
  • Pay Scale ₹90,000 – ₹2,40,000: CTC Approx. ₹34.81 Lakh per annum
  • Pay Scale ₹1,20,000 – ₹2,80,000: CTC Approx. ₹49.30 Lakh per annum

Age Limit (as on 25-03-2026)

  • Engineer Posts (2.9 to 2.12): Maximum Age – 25 Years

  • Experienced Professionals (3.1 to 3.29): Maximum age varies from 26 to 47 years depending upon the position and completed years of experience as per the table in the notification.
  • FTC – Senior Cyber Security Strategist & Advisor (4.1): Maximum Age – 39 to 45 Years (depending on experience)

    • SC / ST candidates: 5 years relaxation
    • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates: 3 years relaxation
    • PwBD (UR): 10 years relaxation
    • PwBD (OBCNC): 13 years relaxation
    • PwBD (SC/ST): 15 years relaxation

    • Ex-Servicemen & Commissioned Officers: 5 years relaxation (subject to conditions)
    • Maximum upper age of applicants shall not exceed 56 years including all possible age relaxations.

Application Fee

  • UR / OBCNC / EWS Candidates: ₹1180/- (Application Fee of ₹1000/- + GST @18% i.e. ₹180/-) + Payment Gateway Charges if any. Non-Refundable.
  • SC / ST / PwBD Candidates: Exempted from payment of application fee.
  • Payment Mode: Debit Card / Credit Card / UPI / Net Banking (Online only).
  • On successful payment, status will change to "Your Transaction is successfully completed".
  • Candidates must ensure payment status is "Completed".
  • Application fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.
  • No other mode of payment than those mentioned above will be accepted.

Important Dates

Event Date
Commencement of Online Application 25th February 2026 (1300 hours onwards)
Last Date of Online Application 25th March 2026 (Up to 2359 hours)
Computer Based Test (CBT) (Tentative) 3rd May 2026

Selection Process

  • The selection process may comprise of various shortlisting and selection tools such as Computer Based Test (CBT) / Written Test / Typing Test, Group Task, Psychometric Assessment, Skill Test, Moot Court, Personal/Technical Interview, Physical Fitness Efficiency Test (if applicable) etc., depending upon the position requirement.
  • Computer Based Test (CBT): Consists of objective questions (subjective as well for Legal HR Officers) and comprises two parts:
    • Part I – General Aptitude: English Language, Quantitative Aptitude Test & Intellectual Potential Test (Logical Reasoning and Data Interpretation).
    • Part II – Technical / Professional Knowledge: Questions related to qualifying degree / educational background required for the applied position.
  • CBT will be conducted tentatively on 3rd May 2026. HPCL reserves the right to reschedule the date of CBT.
  • Questions will be based on syllabus hosted on Careers Page on corporate website (indicative, not exhaustive).
  • Candidates qualifying in CBT, in order of merit and predetermined ratio, will be advised to upload supporting documents for certain positions.
  • Shortlisted candidates will be called for Group Task and/or Personal Interview based on scrutiny of application, uploaded documents, and merit list.
  • Candidates' document verification shall be conducted before Personal Interviews.
  • Candidates may be required to undergo Psychometric Assessments before/after Group Task/Personal Interview.
  • Candidates must secure minimum qualifying marks in each applicable selection stage (CBT, Group Task, and Personal Interview) to be considered for further selection.
  • A category and discipline-wise merit list will be drawn for all candidates who qualify in all applicable stages.
  • The selected candidates would be required to join HPCL as per the date of joining mentioned in the Offer of Appointment.

General Information / Instructions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • All computations of age / relevant experience / qualification shall be done with respect to the last date of receipt of online application i.e. 25th March 2026.
  • All qualifications should be full-time regular courses from AICTE approved / UGC recognized University / Deemed University.
  • Teaching & Research experience in an academic institute will not be considered as relevant work experience.
  • Candidates currently employed at HPCL are not eligible to apply for Lateral Positions (positions where minimum experience is sought).
  • Selected candidates will be on Probation for one year from the Date of Joining.
  • Selected candidates will have to execute a service bond to serve the corporation for a minimum period of three years. Bond Amount: General – ₹3,00,000/-; EWS/OBC(NC)/SC/ST/PwBD – ₹50,000/-.
  • A Retention Amount of ₹5,000/- per month will be deducted for Pay Scales ₹30,000–1,20,000 or ₹40,000–1,40,000 during the first 12 months of probation.
  • A Retention Amount of ₹8,000/- per month will be deducted for Pay Scales from ₹50,000–1,60,000 till ₹90,000–2,40,000 during the first 12 months of probation.
  • Appointment is subject to candidate being medically fit as per standards prescribed by the Corporation.
  • Candidates would be required to clear Physical Fitness Efficiency Test (PFET) comprising Working at Height Test, Endurance Test, and Agility Test after PEME (wherever applicable).
  • Depending upon the requirement of the Corporation, selected candidates can be placed anywhere in India or overseas at the discretion of the Management.
  • Maximum upper age of applicants shall not exceed 56 years including all possible age relaxations.
  • Court of jurisdiction for any dispute will be at Mumbai.
  • Any further corrigendum / addendum would be uploaded only on www.hindustanpetroleum.com.

How to Apply

  • Online Application will be accepted from 1300 hrs on 25th February 2026 till 2359 hrs on 25th March 2026.
  • Candidates are requested to apply online only at www.hindustanpetroleum.com → Careers → Current Openings, after reading the detailed advertisement.
  • No other means / mode of application shall be accepted.
  • Applications with incomplete / wrong particulars or not in the prescribed format will not be considered.
  • The email ID and mobile number provided in the online application should remain valid for at least one year. Applications with pseudo / fake email IDs will attract appropriate action under the law.
  • Upload the photograph and signature of the candidate during application. In case of wrong / missing photo / signature, the candidature will be cancelled.
  • All details given in the online form will be treated as final and no changes will be entertained.
  • Pay the applicable application fee online via Debit Card / Credit Card / UPI / Net Banking and ensure the payment status shows "Completed". Take a printout of the acknowledgment of payment for future reference.
  • Queries must be emailed with subject formatted as "Position Name – Application Number" at [email protected].
  • Candidates are advised to apply online well before the closing date and not wait till the last date.
  • Candidates currently employed in Government Departments / PSUs / Autonomous Bodies must submit their application through proper process and produce No Objection Certificate at the time of Personal Interview.

Selection Process for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

The recruitment consists of 4 successive stages:

Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)

Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for candidates using scribe)

Total Questions: 100 (Each of 1 mark)

Subject Number of Questions
General Science 25
Mathematics 25
General Intelligence and Reasoning 30
General Awareness and Current Affairs 20
TOTAL 100 Questions = 100 Marks

Exam Pattern:

  • Objective type with multiple choices
  • Questions available in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu)
  • Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer
  • Section-wise distribution may vary slightly in actual exam

Minimum Qualifying Marks:

  • UR: 40%
  • EWS: 40%
  • OBC-NCL: 30%
  • SC: 30%
  • ST: 30%
  • PwBD: May be relaxed by 2 marks in case of shortage

Syllabus (Indicative):

  • Mathematics: Number system, BODMAS, Decimals, Fractions, LCM, HCF, Ratio & Proportion, Percentages, Mensuration, Time & Work, Time & Distance, Simple & Compound Interest, Profit & Loss, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Elementary Statistics, Square root, Age Calculations, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
  • General Intelligence & Reasoning: Analogies, Alphabetical & Number Series, Coding & Decoding, Mathematical operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagram, Data Interpretation & Sufficiency, Conclusions & Decision making, Similarities & Differences, Analytical Reasoning, Classification, Directions, Statement-Arguments & Assumptions
  • General Science: Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences of 10th standard level (CBSE)
  • General Awareness & Current Affairs: Science & Technology, Sports, Culture, Personalities, Economics, Politics, and other important subjects

Normalization: Marks will be normalized if CBT conducted in multiple sessions

Stage 2: Physical Efficiency Test (PET)

Shortlisting: 3 times the total vacancies (may vary) based on CBT merit

Nature: Qualifying (Mandatory to pass - marks not counted for final merit)

Candidate Type Test 1: Weight Carrying Test 2: Running
Male Candidates Lift and carry 35 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 4 minutes 15 seconds (in one chance)
Female Candidates Lift and carry 20 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 5 minutes 40 seconds (in one chance)
Transgender Candidates Same relaxed standards as Female candidates

Important PET Notes:

  • Two-stage test: First weight carrying, then running (after recovery gap)
  • Failing in weight carrying means elimination (no running test)
  • Weight carrying involves lifting sandbag (without handle) from waist-height bench and carrying without dropping
  • Candidates' responsibility to ensure medical fitness for PET - Railways not responsible for injuries
  • Exemptions from PET:
    • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) - must pass medical examination
    • Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAA)
    • Ex-Servicemen (ExSM)
  • Pregnant Candidates: Must submit self-declaration. If pregnant, PET deferred till 6 weeks post-confinement. Vacancy kept reserved.

Stage 3: Document Verification (DV)

  • Shortlisting: 1:1 ratio of vacancies based on CBT merit + PET qualification
  • Candidates must produce original certificates
  • No additional time given - absence leads to candidature cancellation
  • Scanned copies to be uploaded before DV at https://oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv
  • Certificates must be in English/Hindi (translated version required otherwise)
  • Hard copy of signed application form to be brought

Stage 4: Medical Examination (ME)

  • Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities
  • Must pass requisite medical fitness test as per IRMM
  • Visual acuity standards strictly enforced
  • Medical appeal option available (one final opportunity on payment)
  • Candidates found medically unsuitable will NOT be given alternative appointment

Final Merit & Selection

  • Based on CBT marks (after normalization if applicable)
  • Subject to PET qualification, DV clearance, and medical fitness
  • Post/Railway allotment as per candidate's preference, merit, medical fitness, and vacancy
  • In case of tie: Older candidate ranked higher; if age also same, alphabetical order of name (A to Z)
  • No right to appointment - RRB/RRC only recommends; appointment by Railway Administration

Professor:

  • A minimum of Ten years of teaching experience in university/college as Assistant Professor / Associate Professor / Professor, and / or research experience at equivalent level at the University / National / International Level Institutions with evidence of having successfully guided doctoral candidate. OR
  •  An outstanding professional, having a Ph.D. degree in the relevant / allied / applied disciplines, from any National / International academic institutions, (not included in 'A' above) / industry who has made significant contribution to the knowledge in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, supported by documentary evidence provided he / she has ten years experience

Assistant Professor:

  • A Master's degree with 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point scale wherever grading system is followed) in a concerned / relevant / allied subject from an Indian University, or an equivalent degree from an accredited foreign university by vide UGC circular. AND
  • National Eligibility Test (NET), State Eligibility Test (SET) and State Level Eligibility Test (SLET) will be the minimum criteria for the direct recruitment to the post of Assistant Professor for all higher education institutions.

Associate Professor:

  • A good academic record with a Ph.D. degree in the concerned / allied / relevant disciplines; A Master's Degree with at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade ina point- scale, wherever the grading system is followed); and A minimum of eight years of experience of teaching and / or research in an academic / research position equivalent to that of Assistant Professor in a University, College or Accredited Research National /International Institution / industry with a minimum of seven publications in the peer-reviewed or UGC- listed journals and a total research score of 75 as per the criteria given in Appendix II, Table 2 of Government of Maharashtra's Higher & Technical Education Department's 7 PayCommission Government Resolution No. Misc- 2018/C.R.56/18/UNI- 1, dated 8th March, 2019 and Corrigendum dated 10th May 2019.

Director:

  • A Master's Degree in Library Science/Information Science/Documentation Science with at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in point-scale, wherever grading system is followed;
  • At least ten years as a Librarian at any level in University Library or ten years of teaching as Assistant/Associate Professor in Library Science or ten years' experience as a College Librarian;
  • Evidence of innovative library services, including the integration of ICT in a library; and
  • A Ph.D. Degree in Library Science / Information Science / Documentation Science / Archives and manuscript-keeping.

  • Minimum two years' experience in translation work from English to Hindi and vice-versa in Central Government or State Government offices, including Government organizations or autonomous bodies; OR Minimum two years' experience in terminological work in Hindi and translation work from English to Hindi or Hindi to English, preferably involving technical or scientific literature; OR Experience in teaching, research, writing, or journalism in Hindi, involving regular use of Hindi and/or Hindi-English translation.

In this article, you’ll find the TMC ACTREC Assistant Professor, Consultant and Professor Posts recruitment details, including eligibility criteria, age limit, salary structure, selection process, application steps, and direct links to the official notification and Online application form.

Advertisement

ACTREC Vacancy Details 

Sl. No. Post Name Pay Level No. of Posts Location
1 Professor - Medical Oncology (F) Level 13 1 Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital & Research Centre, Muzaffarpur

Total 20  

Eligibility Criteria

1. Professor - Medical Oncology

  • D.M. or D.N.B. in Medical Oncology or equivalent postgraduate degree recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • Minimum 5 years post D.M./D.N.B. experience in Medical Oncology in a teaching institute.

2. Assistant Professor - Pathology (Tumor Tissue Repository)

  • M.D. or D.N.B. in Pathology or equivalent postgraduate degree recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • Minimum 3 years experience in Tumor Tissue Repository/Tissue Banking/Biorepository with expertise in tissue handling, processing and cryopreservation techniques.
  • Knowledge of bio-banking regulations and biosafety guidelines.

3. Assistant Professor - Radiation Oncology

  • M.D. or D.N.B. in Radiation Oncology/Radiotherapy or equivalent postgraduate degree.
  • 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Radiation Oncology in a teaching hospital or cancer centre.
  • Experience in Brachytherapy, 3D conformal treatment planning and IMRT is desirable.

4. Assistant Professor - Anesthesiology (2 Posts)

  • M.D. or D.N.B. in Anesthesia or equivalent postgraduate degree in Anesthesiology.
  • 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Anesthesia in a teaching hospital.
  • Experience in critical care and pain management is desirable.

5. Assistant Professor - Pathology (3 Posts)

  • D.M. in Oncopathology or Haematopathology, or M.D./D.N.B. in Pathology or equivalent postgraduate degree.
  • Minimum 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Pathology in a teaching hospital.

6. Assistant Professor - Medical Oncology, Solid Tumor (3 Posts)

  • D.M. or D.N.B. in Medical Oncology or equivalent postgraduate degree.
  • 1 year experience in Solid Tumor Medical Oncology in a teaching hospital is desirable.

7. Assistant Professor - Intensivist, Critical Care (2 Posts)

  • D.M. in Critical Care or M.D./D.N.B. in Anaesthesia/General Medicine/Pulmonary Medicine/Pediatrics or equivalent postgraduate degree.
  • For M.D./D.N.B.: 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Critical Care.

8. Assistant Professor - Interventional Radiology (2 Posts)

  • D.M. in Interventional Radiology or M.D./D.N.B. in Radiodiagnosis recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • For M.D./D.N.B.: 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Interventional Radiology.

9. Consultant - Infectious Diseases (2 Posts)

  • D.M. in Infectious Disease, or M.D. Medicine/Pediatrics with Fellowship in Infectious Diseases (minimum 1 year), recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • 3 years post M.D. experience in Infectious Diseases unit.
  • Experience in Transplant Infectious Diseases is desirable.

10. Consultant - Pulmonary Medicine (1 Post)

  • M.D. or D.N.B. in Respiratory Medicine/Pulmonary Medicine, or D.M. in Pulmonary Medicine/Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • For M.D./D.N.B.: Minimum 3 years post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Pulmonary Medicine in a teaching hospital.
  • Skills in EBUS, Medical Thoracoscopy and advanced bronchoscopy procedures are desirable.

11. Consultant - Pathology (2 Posts)

  • M.D. or D.N.B. in Pathology or equivalent postgraduate degree recognized by National Medical Commission.
  • Minimum 1 year post M.D./D.N.B. experience in Pathology in a teaching hospital.

Grade / Level Posts Pay Scale Initial Pay

Level 12 (Grade E) Assistant Professor positions, Consultant posts Rs. 15,600 – 39,100 + GP 7,600 Rs. 78,800/-
Level 11 (Grade D) Consultant - Pathology Rs. 15,600 – 39,100 + GP 6,600 Rs. 67,700/-

Additional Benefits: Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), medical facility, residential accommodation (subject to availability), institutional financial support for medical meetings and conferences after probation, and retirement benefits/pension under New Pension Scheme as per TMC rules.[web:2]

Application Fee

Category Application Fee
General / OBC Candidates Rs. 300/-
SC / ST Candidates Exempted
Female Candidates Exempted
Persons with Disabilities (PwBD) Exempted
Ex-Servicemen (1st time applying) Exempted

Important Dates

Event Date
Notification Release Date 03-02-2026
Online Application Start Date 03-02-2026
Online Application Last Date 04-03-2026 (5:30 PM IST)
Document Verification & Interview As per interview schedule notified later

Selection Process

  • Initial Screening: Applications will be screened based on details filled in the online form and uploaded documents.
  • Interview: Shortlisted candidates will be called for personal interview; there is no written examination for these posts.
  • Document Verification: Candidates must produce original certificates along with photocopies at the time of interview.
  • Final Selection: Final merit list will be prepared based on interview performance and eligibility.

How to Apply for ACTREC Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official ACTREC website: https://actrec.gov.in/.
  2. Go to the “Jobs” or “Recruitment/Career” section and open Advt No. ACTREC/ADVT/A-01/2026 for medical posts. [web:3][web:5]
  3. Click on the “Click here to apply” or “Apply Online” link.
  4. Register (if required) and log in to the recruitment portal.
  5. Fill the online application form carefully with personal, educational and experience details.
  6. Upload scanned copies of required documents (educational certificates, experience certificates, caste/Category/EWS/PwBD certificates, etc.).
  7. Upload recent passport-size photograph and signature as per specifications.
  8. Pay the application fee online (if applicable) using Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI or Net Banking.
  9. Review all entered details and submit the application form before the last date and time.
  10. Download/print the submitted application form and fee receipt for future reference.

Important Instructions

  • Applications will be accepted only through the online portal; offline forms will not be considered.
  • Candidates must ensure they fulfill all eligibility criteria regarding age, qualification and experience before applying.
  • A valid email ID and mobile number must be kept active throughout the recruitment process.
  • Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to avoid last minute server issues.
  • Selected candidates may be rotated to different Tata Memorial Centre units across India as per organizational requirement.
  • Minimum service of 5 years at the initial place of posting is generally required before seeking transfer.
  • TMC/ACTREC reserves the right to make appointments on contract basis with consolidated salary, if required.
  • For any recruitment related queries, candidates can email at [email protected] (phone queries are not entertained).

Selection Process

  • Stage 1: Written Examination (19th July, 2026)
    • Paper-I: General Ability and Intelligence - 250 Marks
      • Duration: 2 hours (10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon)
      • Type: Objective (Multiple Choice) Type questions
      • Medium: English as well as Hindi
      • Subjects: General Mental Ability (logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, numerical ability, data interpretation), General Science, Current Events of National & International Importance, Indian Polity & Economy, History of India, Indian & World Geography
      • There will be penalty (Negative Marking) for wrong answers: One third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question will be deducted for each wrong answer
    • Paper-II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension - 200 Marks
      • Duration: 3 hours (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM)
      • Type: Conventional (Descriptive) Type
      • Part-A: Essay questions (80 Marks) - to be answered in long narrative form either in Hindi or English. Topics: modern Indian history especially freedom struggle, geography, polity and economy, security and human rights issues, analytical ability
      • Part-B: Comprehension, précis writing, other communications/language skills (120 Marks) - to be attempted in English only. Topics: Comprehension passages, précis writing, developing counter arguments, simple grammar and other language testing aspects
      • Candidates must write answers only in the medium allowed. No credit for answers written in other medium
    • There will be minimum qualifying marks separately in each Paper as may be fixed by the Commission
    • Paper-I will be evaluated first and Paper-II will be evaluated only for those who obtain minimum qualifying marks in Paper-I
  • Stage 2: Physical Standards Tests (PST) / Physical Efficiency Tests (PET)
    • Conducted for candidates qualified in Written Examination
    • Physical Standards Requirements:
      • Men: Height 165 cm, Chest 81 cm (unexpanded) with 5 cm minimum expansion, Weight 50 kg
      • Women: Height 157 cm, Weight 46 kg
      • Height and chest measurement will be measured correct to one decimal in centimeter
      • Weight should be as per height and age as per prescribed chart
    • Physical Efficiency Tests:
      • Men: 100 Meter Race in 16 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 3 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.5 Meters (3 Chances), Shot Put (7.26 Kg) 4.5 Meters (3 Chances)
      • Women: 100 Meter Race in 18 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 4 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.0 Meters (3 Chances)
    • Female candidates must submit self-declaration about pregnancy status before PST/PET
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Stage 3: Interview / Personality Test
    • Only for candidates qualified in PST/PET
    • Marks: 150 Marks
    • Conducted by Union Public Service Commission
    • Candidates declared unqualified in PET will not be called for Interview
    • NCC 'B' or 'C' Certificate holders will be given consideration at Interview stage
  • Stage 4: Medical Standards Tests (MST)
    • Conducted only for candidates who appeared in Interview/Personality Test
    • Detailed Medical Standards prescribed for Eye Sight, Ear, Nose, Neck, Teeth, General Health, etc.
    • Eye Sight: Better eye 6/6 or 6/9 (corrected), Worse eye 6/12 or 6/9 (corrected), Near Vision N6/N9 (corrected), Colour Perception CP-III by ISIHARA plates
    • LASIK surgery correction permitted subject to prescribed criteria
    • Candidates declared 'UNFIT' can appear before Review Medical Board preferably next day of DME
    • Appeals against MST results must be made within 24 hours after declaration of DME results
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Final Selection/Merit:
    • Merit list drawn on basis of marks obtained in Written Examination and Interview/Personality Test
    • Any candidate found not satisfying prescribed Medical Standards after MST will not be appointed
    • Tie Breaking Principle: (i) Higher marks in written total, (ii) Higher marks in Paper-I, (iii) Senior in age, (iv) At Commission's discretion
